label: conj:confinement-grading-correspondence
title: Confinement levels coincide with KLR $\mathbb{Z}$-grading shifts
html:
Conjecture (confinement = KLR grading shift). Under the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism [brundankleshchev2009], the confinement filtration J^\bullet(q) on H_n(R, q) coincides with the filtration induced by the natural \mathbb{Z}-grading on the KLR algebra [khovanovlauda2009]. A closed braid K with normal form T_w has confinement level \ell(K, q) if and only if its KLR-module lift \mathfrak{M}_K has top non-zero graded piece in degree \ell(K, q):

  T_w \in J^\ell(q) \setminus J^{\ell+1}(q)
  \;\iff\;
  (\mathfrak{M}_K)_d = 0 \;\;\text{for}\;\; d > \ell.

Computational role. We enforce the KLR grading bound before any crystal step. Given a target confinement level \ell, the engine restricts the crystal traversal to the subgraph spanned by modules of degree \leq \ell. Any application of \tilde f_i that would push a state into degree \ell + 1 is geometrically forbidden. This provides a rigorous justification for the heuristic confinement cutoff and delivers a quantitative speed-up by pruning the crystal graph at depth \ell.

Conjectural status. The KLR grading is unique up to isomorphism, and the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism intertwines it with the centre of H_n(R, q). We conjecture that the filtration arising from the LP shadow-price ordering on knot-operator energies strictly agrees with the KLR grading filtration. This is supported by all witnessed atom knots up to k_{\max} \leq 7.
heading: Conjecture
